## Objective

Prove the decisive \(K_2\)--\(K_1\)--outer matching theorem for the
positive-parameter algebraic channel.

## Proof obligations

- [ ] Construct the outer compactification and a parameter-dependent
      codimension-one future-staying invariant hypersurface.
- [ ] Prove normal expansion and third-order bunching in intrinsic quotient
      norms.
- [ ] Fix common physical matching sections and chart transitions.
- [ ] Construct the endpoint-anchored adjoint row.
- [ ] Prove that the exchange coefficient is nonzero.
- [ ] Derive and uniformly invert the finite-dimensional matching operator.
- [ ] Control two external parameter derivatives without shifted-base-point or
      trace loss.
- [ ] Prove that the matched sheet converges to the central algebraic sheet in
      the norm required by the first-hit theorem.
- [ ] Prove covariance of the truncated action when the matching cut moves.

## Mathematical stop condition

This is the first kill point for the full two-end project.  A genuine blockage
requires a proof that the exchange vanishes structurally, that no appropriate
normally expanding outer hypersurface exists, or that every admissible directed
matching formulation necessarily has an unbounded interface operator.  A hard
estimate or failed code path is not a blockage.

If genuinely blocked, open the finite-cut fallback theorem and mark the
two-end target as obstructed rather than silently replacing the end.
